- F01: South Korea is considering sending military resources to the Strait of Hormuz to support freedom of navigation. (Source: France 24)
- F02: The US is investigating whether a missile hit an Iranian wedding celebration where at least four people were killed. (Source: BBC)
- F03: The US has not targeted civilians in its military operation in the Strait of Hormuz. (Source: BBC)
- F04: South Korea could contribute to the US security effort in the Strait of Hormuz. (Source: France 24)
- F05: Iran has claimed that an American missile hit a wedding celebration in the Strait of Hormuz, which would be a war crime. (Source: BBC)

The core question: South Korea prepares for military deployment in the Strait of Hormuz.

The main story is about South Korea considering/preparing a military deployment to the Strait of Hormuz. The BBC claims about the missile/wedding are related context — the US military involvement in the Hormuz area and allegations about civilian casualties.

I should attribute this properly: "ifølge USA" or "USA afviser..." Actually the claim as stated is "USA har ikke målrettet civile" — this is likely a US assertion. Vance said the US is investigating whether a missile hit an Iranian wedding. So the US position is that they don't target civilians. The source headline says "US investigating if missile hit Iran wedding, Vance says". So Vance is the one saying the US is investigating. The claim F03 "USA har ikke målrettet civile i sin militære indsats" — attributed to S2 (BBC). I can write "USA har ifølge BBC oplyst..." or better: attribute to US statements as reported by BBC. Let me be careful: I can say "Ifølge BBC har USA oplyst, at det ikke har målrettet civile..." That preserves attribution.

F05: Iran has claimed that an American missile hit a wedding celebration in the Strait of Hormuz, which would be a war crime.
